subject: Re: ClearHealth VPC inference queue backlog and SLA impact
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearHealth Oncall <oncall@clearhealth.io>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: VPC inference queue backlog causing 504s and throughput regressions

Hi Priyom,

We're seeing a sustained backlog on our Redwood private VPC cluster starting ~12:40 PDT which has produced a spike in 504s for /v1/generate and a P95 jump from 300ms to ~2.4s for short prompt traffic. Throughput (requests/sec) for our peak pool has dropped ~30% despite stable upstream traffic. Error rates climbed to 4.8% and we've disabled non-critical pipelines to keep the product usable.

Attached is a tar with kernel traces and the inference traces (inference_traces_clearhealth_0831.json). Engineers flagged repeated "kv_cache_miss" GC stalls and a backlog on the request queue that grows during 1s bursts. This is impacting our ambulatory scheduling customers — we need urgent help.

What we need from Redwood:
- Immediate triage (logs + recommended short-term mitigations we can apply without a full restart)
- Guidance on safe canary/rolling update strategy if a config change is required
- Estimated time-to-fix and whether this will require scheduled downtime
- Credit for SLA impact (we will escalate internally if no action)

Thanks,
Alex Rivera
Head of Platform Engineering
ClearHealth
[Attachment: kernel_logs_20270831.tar.gz (1.2MB)]
[Attachment: inference_traces_clearhealth_0831.json (650KB)]

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC inference queue backlog causing 504s and throughput regressions

Alex —

Thanks for the heads up and the traces. I'm opening a high-priority incident on our side and looping in SRE (Neha) and your account lead (Marissa). We'll triage immediately. Proposed immediate next steps:

1) Nudge for a 30-min triage call now to review traces (joining links below)
2) Neha will review kernel and kv cache traces and propose a conservative mitigation we can apply without restarting prod (e.g., temporary batching caps / prefix caching adjustments)
3) We'll prepare a written canary plan for any restart or config change (no full-prod reboot without your signoff)
4) I'll coordinate any credit request with our finance/ops team and loop in leadership if escalation is required

Can you confirm whether you can accept a rolling update to a single replica in the affected pool during US overnight if we recommend it? If not, we'll prioritize a hotfix path.

Joining: 14:35 PDT / 21:35Z — dial-in in calendar invite.

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
priom.das@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0132

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 31 Aug 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: RE: VPC inference queue backlog causing 504s and throughput regressions

Alex / Priyom —

Quick notes from initial triage (first 30m):
- Observed repeated large KV cache evictions that correlate with the P95 spikes. Eviction rate jumps during short bursts (1-2s) and KV cache rebuilds are stalling token generation loops.
- GPU utilization across the pool is NOT saturated (60-70%) but CPU-side worker threads are seeing sustained sys time spikes (context-switch + io-wait).
- We see interleaved stack traces pointing to preemption in the runtime's background KV GC and a few kernel warnings for 'page_fault' during heavy KV rehydrate.

Short-term mitigations we can apply (no full restart):
- Reduce max_batch_tokens on the affected route from 2048 -> 1024 to reduce KV pressure (can be rolled per-route)
- Temporarily enable prefix-only KV caching for the route to avoid full-kv rebuilds
- Throttle background KV GC during your peak windows (config toggle)
If you can tolerate a single-replica rolling update, we can also push a micro-release with a KV rehydration backoff fix that prevents synchronous rebuilds on miss (low risk, canary-able). That would require ~15-20s to restart a single replica and a canary sequence across replicas (~10-15 minutes total).

I attached the preliminary inference traces with annotated points. If the customer cannot accept restarts in prod, we should apply the config mitigations above immediately and monitor.

—Neha
SRE Lead, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: inference_traces_clearhealth_0831_annotated.json]

From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: ClearHealth Oncall <oncall@clearhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 02:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: VPC inference queue backlog causing 504s and throughput regressions

Thanks, Neha and team. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing the annotated traces:
- The affected pool serves both staging and prod, but prod is mission-critical. We cannot accept any restart that drops >1 replica at once. Rolling update / canary is acceptable if you can guarantee no more than one replica offline at a time.
- If configuration toggles fix the immediate spikes we'll take that and avoid restarts. Please apply the three mitigations in the next 30 minutes and report back with delta metrics (P95 / error rate / queue depth).
- Our execs are pushing for concrete SLA remediation — please provide an initial credit estimate for the impacted window (we expect formal request).

Also: attaching one of the kernel traces we pulled from the worker that experienced a hard stall. If you think this is an OS/kernel-level misconfiguration vs runtime, let us know since we may need to coordinate with infra.

—Alex
[Attachment: worker_trace_0819.txt]

From: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Escalation: ClearHealth prod P95 spike + SLA exposure (CLH-4592)

LAuren/Leadership —

I need immediate exec attention on ClearHealth (CLH-4592). Summary:
- Impact: Production P95 increased from ~300ms to ~2.4s and error rates peaked at 4.8% during the backlog window (2027-08-31 19:40 - 20:15Z).
- Cause (triage in progress): KV cache eviction/rebuild stalls in our runtime leading to request queue backlog; candidate mitigations available without restart (see Neha's list).
- Customer constraints: Cannot accept multi-replica downtime; will accept single-replica rolling canary if we guarantee controlled restarts.

Recommended asks from leadership:
1) Approve customer-facing credit estimate pre-emptively so we can respond to Alex's execs quickly. I propose a provisional credit: 50% of hosting fees for the impacted 35-minute window, capped at $15k. (Marissa, can finance ops sign-off?)
2) Approve SRE hotfix deployment via rolling canary (Neha: you estimate 60-90m end-to-end including validation).
3) Assign an executive to the customer sync at 17:00 PDT today if ClearHealth requests one.

I've attached a quick proposed credit calc sheet and the incident runbook link.

—Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: proposed_credit_calc_CLH-4592.xlsx]

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@clearhealth.io>
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Escalation: ClearHealth prod P95 spike + SLA exposure (CLH-4592)

Team —

Thanks for the rapid triage and clear recommendation. I approve the provisional remediation plan:

- Apply Neha's non-restart config mitigations immediately (reduce max_batch_tokens, enable prefix-only KV, throttle KV GC). Monitor for 30 minutes.
- If mitigations do not return P95 within acceptable bounds, proceed with a single-replica rolling canary hotfix. SRE to coordinate canary schedule with customer and provide explicit rollback criteria.
- Approve provisional customer credit: 50% of hosting fees for the 35-minute impact period, capped at $15,000. Finance (Marissa) to confirm back-office capture and make the credit visible on the next invoice.

Priyom: please coordinate an exec sync with ClearHealth if they request it and send a one-paragraph customer-facing summary after mitigation. Neha: prioritize the canary path but only proceed after customer acknowledgement.

—Lauren Bishop
VP, Customer Success, Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwood.ai | +1 (650) 555-0188
